title: L6 — THE INVISIBLE FEE
voice: Your broker charges you a fee they never put on the screen. You paid it the second you entered — before the market even moved. Most traders never find it. Here's exactly where it hides.
Because the price you were watching isn't one price. It's two. One to buy, one to sell. They're never the same. The gap between them is called the spread — and the moment you enter, you pay it.

That cost, at least, is written down. You can see it before you click. But there's a second cost nobody shows you. Between the instant you click and the instant you're filled, the price moves. Where you aimed and where you land are not the same place.

That gap has a name: slippage. In a calm market, it's tiny — a rounding error. But when everything moves fast, the gap opens wide, right as you try to cross it. And it's biggest at the exact moment you can least afford it.
You can't refuse either fee. The spread and the slippage are the cost of the door. But you can count them. Because if you don't know what entering costs, you don't know what winning has to beat.

caption:
You entered a trade. You did nothing else. And you're already down. Here's why — and it's not bad luck.

There are two invisible costs every trade pays. One is written down. The other isn't — and it's biggest exactly when you can least afford it.

Comment "LINE" for the full series on how trading actually works underneath.

THE LINE — the proof is on the chart.
